Each is one line in :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.GLOBAL_THRESHOLDS` or :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.LOCAL_THRESHOLDS`, and everything around the level -- the smoothing, the threshold correction, the bright or dark side, filling holes, the watershed split, the border rule, the minimum area -- is the code Otsu already went through. records.translation: Cada algoritmo de umbral de este módulo solo elige el nivel del umbral. Cada uno es una línea en :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.GLOBAL_THRESHOLDS` o :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.LOCAL_THRESHOLDS`, y todo lo que rodea al nivel -- el suavizado, la corrección del umbral, el lado claro u oscuro, el relleno de huecos, la división por watershed, la regla del borde, el área mínima -- es el código por el que ya pasaba Otsu. Elegir Li en lugar de Otsu cambia de dónde procede un número y nada más.

records.context: Some thresholds are not offered here. Local mean and local Gaussian thresholding are not offered again: they are the Adaptive threshold mode, which runs the organelle engine's ``adaptive`` branch with a block size and an offset. Local OTSU is not offered again either: it is the "Local threshold (uneven illumination)" switch in plain Otsu mode, used by whole-image detection. Other named thresholds ignore saved Local Otsu and class-count settings; Multi-Otsu alone uses the selected class count and band in both scopes. Plain Otsu retains its legacy magnifier preprocessing, while the other thresholds use the whole-image engine on the requested extracted image region. Niblack uses ``T = m - k*s``; Sauvola uses ``T = m*(1 + k*(s/R - 1))``, where ``m`` and ``s`` are the local mean and standard deviation. The engine supplies float32 values without rescaling their range, so scikit-image's default Sauvola ``R`` is 1. These formulas are different, and changing the intensity scale can change Sauvola's result.
records.label: spacr.qt.cpu_modes#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Some thresholds are not offered here. Local mean and local Gaussian thresholding are not offered again: they are the Adaptive threshold mode, which runs the organelle engine's ``adaptive`` branch with a block size and an offset. Local OTSU is not offered again either: it is the "Local threshold (uneven illumination)" switch in plain Otsu mode, used by whole-image detection. Other named thresholds ignore saved Local Otsu and class-count settings; Multi-Otsu alone uses the selected class count and band in both scopes. Plain Otsu retains its legacy magnifier preprocessing, while the other thresholds use the whole-image engine on the requested crop. Niblack uses ``T = m - k*s``; Sauvola uses ``T = m*(1 + k*(s/R - 1))``, where ``m`` and ``s`` are the local mean and standard deviation. The engine supplies float32 values without rescaling their range, so scikit-image's default Sauvola ``R`` is 1. These formulas are different, and changing the intensity scale can change Sauvola's result.
records.translation: Algunos umbrales no se ofrecen aquí. Los umbrales de media local y gaussiano local no se vuelven a ofrecer: son el modo de umbral Adaptive, que ejecuta la rama ``adaptive`` del motor de orgánulos con un tamaño de bloque y un desplazamiento. Tampoco se vuelve a ofrecer el OTSU local: es el conmutador "Local threshold (uneven illumination)" del modo Otsu simple, que usa la detección sobre la imagen completa. Los demás umbrales con nombre ignoran los ajustes guardados de Local Otsu y de número de clases; solo Multi-Otsu usa el número de clases y la banda seleccionados en ambos ámbitos. El Otsu simple conserva su preprocesamiento heredado de la lupa, mientras que los demás umbrales usan el motor de imagen completa sobre el recorte solicitado. Niblack usa ``T = m - k*s``; Sauvola usa ``T = m*(1 + k*(s/R - 1))``, donde ``m`` y ``s`` son la media y la desviación estándar locales. El motor proporciona valores float32 sin reescalar su intervalo, de modo que el ``R`` predeterminado de Sauvola en scikit-image es 1. Estas fórmulas son distintas, y cambiar la escala de intensidad puede cambiar el resultado de Sauvola.

records.context: the Gaussian blur before the maxima are found, in pixels. Leave the chain's denoise off unless the microscope field of view is genuinely noisy, or the two blurs compound.

This is separate from the image enhancement chain's denoise, which has already run by the time a detector sees the image: the blur that gives one object one centre is usually much stronger than the blur wanted for measuring the object's edge, and the propagation measures the edge on the same blurred image. records.translation: el desenfoque gaussiano previo a la búsqueda de máximos, en píxeles. Es independiente de la eliminación de ruido de la cadena de mejora de imagen, que ya se ha ejecutado cuando un detector ve la imagen: el desenfoque que da a un objeto un único centro suele ser mucho más fuerte que el deseado para medir el borde del objeto, y la propagación mide el borde sobre la misma imagen desenfocada. Deje desactivada la eliminación de ruido de la cadena salvo que el campo tenga realmente ruido, o los dos desenfoques se acumularán.

Morphology and split act on a detector's labels and are Make Masks' own; a plate run's Cellpose labels are not reshaped by them. The Mask settings ``remove_background``, ``background`` and ``signal_to_noise`` are per-channel intensity floors applied by normalization afterwards, and :func:`spacr.object._preprocess_batch` is the organelle batches' own rolling ball and CLAHE; neither is configured here.

records.context: Found through ``findChildren`` rather than by walking the menu bar's actions and calling ``QAction.menu()``. That reading is the obvious one and it does not survive on PySide6 6.11: the QMenu wrapper it returns is only valid while the QAction wrapper it came off is alive, so the menu went stale the moment this function returned — "Internal C++ object (PySide6.QtWidgets.QMenu) already deleted" on the very next line — and keeping the owners alive as attributes segfaulted during the next event dispatch instead. ``findChildren`` hands back children the menu bar owns in C++, which stay valid for as long as the window does.
records.label: spacr.qt.first_run.find_menu#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Found through ``findChildren`` rather than by walking the menu bar's actions and calling ``QAction.menu()``. That reading is the obvious one and it does not survive on PySide6 6.11: the QMenu wrapper it returns is only valid while the QAction wrapper it came off is alive, so the menu went stale the moment this function returned — "Internal C++ object (PySide6.QtWidgets.QMenu) already deleted" on the very next line — and keeping the owners alive as attributes segfaulted during the next event dispatch instead. ``findChildren`` hands back children the menu bar owns in C++, which stay valid for as long as the window does.
records.translation: Se encuentra mediante ``findChildren`` en lugar de recorrer las acciones de la barra de menús y llamar a ``QAction.menu()``. Esa lectura es la obvia y no funciona en PySide6 6.11: el envoltorio QMenu que devuelve solo es válido mientras siga vivo el envoltorio QAction del que procede, de modo que el menú quedaba obsoleto en cuanto esta función volvía — "Internal C++ object (PySide6.QtWidgets.QMenu) already deleted" en la línea siguiente — y mantener vivos los propietarios como atributos provocaba en cambio un fallo de segmentación durante el siguiente envío de eventos. ``findChildren`` devuelve hijos que la barra de menús posee en C++, que siguen siendo válidos mientras exista la ventana.

records.source: Those two lines, in that order, are reproduced exactly by ``tests/qt/test_gc_runs_on_the_gui_thread.py`` with no spaCR code involved at all: build a QObject that owns a *running* QTimer, drop it into a reference CYCLE so only the collector can free it, then call ``gc.collect()`` from a worker thread. The collector runs the destructor **on whichever thread it happens to be running on**, and Qt cannot stop a timer from there.
records.translation: Esas dos líneas, en ese orden, las reproduce exactamente ``tests/qt/test_gc_runs_on_the_gui_thread.py`` sin que intervenga ningún código de spaCR: construir un QObject que posee un QTimer *en ejecución*, meterlo en un CICLO de referencias para que solo el recolector pueda liberarlo y después llamar a ``gc.collect()`` desde un hilo de trabajo. El recolector ejecuta el destructor **en el hilo en el que esté ejecutándose en ese momento**, y Qt no puede detener un temporizador desde allí.

records.context: The defect is not specific to the preview. CPython runs an automatic collection whenever an allocation pushes a generation past its threshold, so the collection executes on the independent execution path that allocated most recently. A Cellpose pass allocates heavily in a background execution unit, so that worker is the likely independent execution path to execute the collection and therefore to destroy unrelated widgets the main GUI execution path released earlier. The resulting crash is timing-dependent, occurs away from the code that created the cycle, and names no file.

records.source: The ratio belongs to the screen, not the application, and a window can be dragged from a retina laptop onto an ordinary external monitor. A picture rendered at 2x and moved to a 1x screen is merely wasteful; the reverse is blurry. :func:`follow_device_ratio` subscribes a widget to the change Qt already sends, for the pictures whose source is still in memory and whose re-render is a single call. Pictures scaled inside ``paintEvent`` need nothing: they ask for the ratio again on the next frame.
records.translation: La relación pertenece a la pantalla, no a la aplicación, y una ventana puede arrastrarse desde un portátil con pantalla retina a un monitor externo normal. Una imagen representada a 2x y movida a una pantalla 1x solo es un desperdicio; lo contrario queda borroso. :func:`follow_device_ratio` suscribe un widget al cambio que Qt ya envía, para las imágenes cuyo origen sigue en memoria y cuya nueva representación es una sola llamada. Las imágenes escaladas dentro de ``paintEvent`` no necesitan nada: vuelven a pedir la relación en el siguiente fotograma.

records.context: ``QPixmap.scaled(w, h, ...)`` takes DEVICE pixels but every caller in a GUI means LOGICAL ones -- the size the picture should occupy on application view. On a display with a device pixel ratio of 2, which is every retina Mac and plenty of Windows and Linux machines, Qt then stretches that logical bitmap across twice as many real pixels in each direction: a 200 px render blown up to 400 px, from a 3334 px source. The picture is not low-resolution; the scaling threw the resolution away.
records.label: spacr.qt.hidpi#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``QPixmap.scaled(w, h, ...)`` takes DEVICE pixels but every caller in a GUI means LOGICAL ones -- the size the picture should occupy on screen. On a display with a device pixel ratio of 2, which is every retina Mac and plenty of Windows and Linux machines, Qt then stretches that logical bitmap across twice as many real pixels in each direction: a 200 px render blown up to 400 px, from a 3334 px source. The picture is not low-resolution; the scaling threw the resolution away.
records.translation: ``QPixmap.scaled(w, h, ...)`` recibe píxeles del DISPOSITIVO, pero todos los llamadores de una GUI se refieren a píxeles LÓGICOS -- el tamaño que debe ocupar la imagen en pantalla. En una pantalla con una relación de píxeles del dispositivo de 2, que es el caso de todos los Mac con pantalla retina y de muchas máquinas Windows y Linux, Qt estira entonces ese mapa de bits lógico sobre el doble de píxeles reales en cada dirección: una representación de 200 px ampliada a 400 px, a partir de un original de 3334 px. La imagen no es de baja resolución; el escalado desechó la resolución.

records.source: A rule applied by hand at each site holds until the next site is written, so what ships is :func:`scaled_for` -- source, widget, logical size -- and every call site asking it. The next picture is then right without its author knowing this problem exists.

records.context: The rules:
records.label: spacr.qt.job_runner#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rules:
records.translation: Las reglas:

records.context: **QObject receiver requirement.** Connect ``QThread.finished`` to a method on a QObject that belongs to the GUI thread. A closure is unsafe. PySide6 assigns the QThread itself as a closure's receiver. :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` first connects ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``. Slots execute in connection order. DeferredDelete is therefore posted before the closure callback. Qt discards the queued callback after destroying its receiver. The job then remains active and ``active_jobs()`` never reaches zero.
records.label: spacr.qt.job_runner#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``QThread.finished`` must be connected to a **bound method of a GUI-thread QObject**, never a closure. PySide6 makes the QThread itself the receiver for a closure, and :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` connects ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater`` first. Slots run in connection order, so the DeferredDelete is posted ahead of the closure's metacall and Qt discards queued events for a destroyed receiver: the job is never retired and ``active_jobs()`` never returns to zero.
records.translation: ``QThread.finished`` debe conectarse a un **método enlazado de un QObject del hilo de la GUI**, nunca a un cierre léxico. PySide6 convierte al propio QThread en el receptor de un cierre léxico, y :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` conecta primero ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``. Los slots se ejecutan en el orden de conexión, de modo que el DeferredDelete se publica antes que la metallamada del cierre léxico, y Qt descarta los eventos en cola de un receptor destruido: la tarea nunca se retira y ``active_jobs()`` nunca vuelve a cero.

records.context: A strong reference to both the QThread and the worker must be held until ``thread.finished``. A QThread garbage-collected while executing aborts the process.
records.label: spacr.qt.job_runner#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A strong reference to both the QThread and the worker must be held until ``thread.finished``. A QThread garbage-collected while running aborts the process.
records.translation: Debe mantenerse una referencia fuerte tanto al QThread como al proceso de trabajo hasta ``thread.finished``. Un QThread recolectado como basura mientras se ejecuta aborta el proceso.

records.context: Only the last one is live, and it moves nothing: the application sheet carries 49 hardcoded ``font-size: <N>px`` declarations, and a QSS font-size beats the inherited application font.
records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Only the last one is live, and it moves nothing: the application sheet carries 49 hardcoded ``font-size: <N>px`` declarations, and a QSS font-size beats the inherited application font.
records.translation: Solo el último es en directo, y no mueve nada: la hoja de la aplicación contiene 49 declaraciones ``font-size: <N>px`` fijadas en el código, y un font-size de QSS prevalece sobre la fuente heredada de la aplicación.

records.context: The escape the instruction proposed does not exist. Part 2 of 378 assumed the 49 declarations could be rewritten in ``em`` or ``%`` so that one ``setFont`` moved everything. Qt does not implement either for ``font-size``: ``QCss`` accepts only ``pt``, ``px`` and the CSS size keywords, and silently drops any other unit, so ``font-size: 2em`` leaves the widget at the inherited size. Measured on this PySide6, and pinned by ``test_qt_still_has_no_relative_font_size``, which fails the day Qt gains the unit and makes the simpler design available.
records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: THE ESCAPE THE INSTRUCTION PROPOSED DOES NOT EXIST. Part 2 of 378 assumed the 49 declarations could be rewritten in ``em`` or ``%`` so that one ``setFont`` moved everything. Qt does not implement either for ``font-size``: ``QCss`` accepts only ``pt``, ``px`` and the CSS size keywords, and silently drops any other unit, so ``font-size: 2em`` leaves the widget at the inherited size. Measured on this PySide6, and pinned by ``test_qt_still_has_no_relative_font_size``, which fails the day Qt gains the unit and makes the simpler design available.
records.translation: LA SALIDA QUE PROPONÍA LA INSTRUCCIÓN NO EXISTE. La parte 2 de 378 suponía que las 49 declaraciones podían reescribirse en ``em`` o ``%`` para que un solo ``setFont`` lo moviera todo. Qt no implementa ninguna de las dos para ``font-size``: ``QCss`` solo acepta ``pt``, ``px`` y las palabras clave de tamaño de CSS, y descarta en silencio cualquier otra unidad, de modo que ``font-size: 2em`` deja el widget con el tamaño heredado. Medido en esta versión de PySide6 y fijado por ``test_qt_still_has_no_relative_font_size``, que fallará el día en que Qt incorpore la unidad y haga posible el diseño más sencillo.

records.context: What is live instead. An explicit ``QWidget.setFont`` *does* beat the application sheet's ``font-size`` -- it is the same escape hatch that lets a per-widget sheet win -- and it costs one font assignment and one relayout rather than a global unpolish/repolish. So a notch snapshots each visible widget's font once, then re-scales every widget from that snapshot by the ratio the wheel has travelled. The role hierarchy survives because each widget is scaled from its own baseline: a 22 px title and a 13 px caption stay in proportion without this module knowing which is which.
records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: WHAT IS LIVE INSTEAD. An explicit ``QWidget.setFont`` *does* beat the application sheet's ``font-size`` -- it is the same escape hatch that lets a per-widget sheet win -- and it costs one font assignment and one relayout rather than a global unpolish/repolish. So a notch snapshots each visible widget's font once, then re-scales every widget from that snapshot by the ratio the wheel has travelled. The role hierarchy survives because each widget is scaled from its own baseline: a 22 px title and a 13 px caption stay in proportion without this module knowing which is which.
records.translation: QUÉ ES EN DIRECTO EN SU LUGAR. Un ``QWidget.setFont`` explícito *sí* prevalece sobre el ``font-size`` de la hoja de la aplicación -- es la misma vía de escape que permite que gane una hoja por widget -- y cuesta una asignación de fuente y una nueva disposición en lugar de un despulido/repulido global. Así, un paso de la rueda toma una instantánea de la fuente de cada widget visible una vez y después reescala cada widget a partir de esa instantánea según la proporción que ha recorrido la rueda. La jerarquía de funciones se conserva porque cada widget se escala desde su propia base: un título de 22 px y una leyenda de 13 px mantienen la proporción sin que este módulo sepa cuál es cuál.

records.source: THE EXPENSIVE HALF, ON PURPOSE. Everything :func:`scaled_px` pins is rebuilt here, in one 587 ms step, rather than twenty times a second while the wheel turns -- which is the compromise chosen over a gesture that stutters. Called when the wheel has been still for :data:`_SETTLE_MS`, when Z comes up, and when the window loses focus with Z still down.
records.translation: LA MITAD COSTOSA, A PROPÓSITO. Todo lo que fija :func:`scaled_px` se reconstruye aquí, en un solo paso de 587 ms, en lugar de veinte veces por segundo mientras gira la rueda -- que es el compromiso elegido frente a un gesto que se entrecorta. Se llama cuando la rueda lleva quieta :data:`_SETTLE_MS`, cuando se suelta Z y cuando la ventana pierde el foco con Z todavía pulsada.

records.translation: Las entradas producidas *mientras* un panel de consola está a mitad de una escritura se descartan. records.context: Two phases:
records.label: spacr.qt.maturity.apply#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two phases:
records.translation: Dos fases:

records.context: 1. :data:`PROMOTIONS` lists applications that were assessed and moved. Applying it repeatedly is safe, and it never *moves an application to a lower stage*. If another component promoted an application further, it stays there. This table represents one assessment; loading it later must not undo a newer assessment. 2. Each registered application absent from all assessment tables and without its own line receives :data:`UNASSESSED_STAGE`. This prevents a new module from inheriting ``stable`` merely because no entry exists. The function writes only empty entries, so it cannot override an author, a plugin, or step 1.
records.label: spacr.qt.maturity.apply#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. :data:`PROMOTIONS` — the apps somebody assessed and moved. Idempotent, and it never *demotes*: a module some other code has already promoted further than this table says stays where it is. That matters because the table is a snapshot of one assessment, and the next assessment should not be silently undone by re-importing this module. 2. Every registered app that is in none of the assessment tables and has no line of its own is written in as :data:`UNASSESSED_STAGE`. This is what stops a new module inheriting ``stable`` from the absence of an entry — see the module docstring. It only ever writes where there is nothing, so it cannot overrule an author, a plugin, or phase 1.
records.translation: 1. :data:`PROMOTIONS` — las aplicaciones que alguien evaluó y cambió de etapa. Es idempotente y nunca *rebaja*: un módulo que otro código ya ha promovido más de lo que indica esta tabla se queda donde está. Eso importa porque la tabla es una instantánea de una evaluación, y la siguiente evaluación no debería deshacerse en silencio al volver a importar este módulo. 2. Cada aplicación registrada que no está en ninguna de las tablas de evaluación y no tiene una línea propia se escribe como :data:`UNASSESSED_STAGE`. Esto es lo que impide que un módulo nuevo herede ``stable`` por la ausencia de una entrada — véase el docstring del módulo. Solo escribe donde no hay nada, por lo que no puede anular a un autor, a un complemento ni a la fase 1.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.translation: Home ya funcionaba así, por el motivo indicado en ``AppTile``: las descripciones llegan a varios cientos de caracteres, y una ventana emergente de ese tamaño tapa la cuadrícula en la que el usuario está eligiendo.

records.context: The hook is ``QEvent.ToolTip`` rather than hover. It fires exactly when Qt has decided to show a tooltip -- after the same delay, at the same moment -- so the description appears when the user expects it, and returning ``True`` from the filter is what stops the popup being drawn. Reimplementing the timing on ``HoverEnter`` would be a second, slightly different delay for the same gesture.
records.label: spacr.qt.module_hints#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The hook is ``QEvent.ToolTip`` rather than hover. It fires exactly when Qt has decided to show a tooltip -- after the same delay, at the same moment -- so the description appears when the user expects it, and returning ``True`` from the filter is what stops the popup being drawn. Reimplementing the timing on ``HoverEnter`` would be a second, slightly different delay for the same gesture.
records.translation: El enganche es ``QEvent.ToolTip`` y no el paso del cursor. Se activa exactamente cuando Qt ha decidido mostrar una información emergente -- tras el mismo retardo, en el mismo momento --, de modo que la descripción aparece cuando el usuario la espera, y devolver ``True`` desde el filtro es lo que impide que se dibuje la ventana emergente. Reimplementar la temporización en ``HoverEnter`` supondría un segundo retardo, ligeramente distinto, para el mismo gesto.

records.context: The OPS sample is the well's last two sites because the engine takes a well's microscope field of view count as its highest site number plus one and fits the round well to that count, so a sample has to include the last site to keep the measured 333-microscope field of view layout; see :func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops`. And it carries no phenotype images, because the phenotype phase aligns anchors spread over the whole well, which a two-microscope field of view sample cannot supply.

records.source: The OPS sample is the well's last two sites because the engine takes a well's field count as its highest site number plus one and fits the round well to that count, so a sample has to include the last site to keep the measured 333-field layout; see :func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops`. And it carries no phenotype images, because the phenotype phase aligns anchors spread over the whole well, which a two-field sample cannot supply.
records.translation: La muestra de OPS son los dos últimos sitios del pocillo, porque el motor toma como número de campos de un pocillo su número de sitio más alto más uno y ajusta el pocillo redondo a ese número, de modo que una muestra tiene que incluir el último sitio para conservar la disposición medida de 333 campos; véase :func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops`. Y no lleva imágenes de fenotipo, porque la fase de fenotipo alinea anclas repartidas por todo el pocillo, que una muestra de dos campos no puede aportar.

That is free for a local disk and it is not free for a network one: measured on one workstation, ``os.path.exists`` on a path under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount with ``timeout=600`` -- had not returned after twenty seconds, because the stat is what triggers the automount and the share was asleep.

records.source: `spacr/qt/widgets/file_list.py` asked `os.path.exists` for every remembered path, on the GUI thread, to colour the missing ones red. That is free for a local disk and it is not free for a network one: measured on one workstation, ``os.path.exists`` on a path under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount with ``timeout=600`` -- had not returned after twenty seconds, because the stat is what triggers the automount and the share was asleep.
records.translation: `spacr/qt/widgets/file_list.py` preguntaba a `os.path.exists` por cada ruta recordada, en el hilo de la GUI, para colorear en rojo las que faltaban. Eso no cuesta nada en un disco local, pero sí en uno de red: medido en una estación de trabajo, ``os.path.exists`` sobre una ruta bajo ``/nas_mnt`` -- un montaje ``autofs`` con ``timeout=600`` -- no había vuelto al cabo de veinte segundos, porque el stat es lo que desencadena el montaje automático y el recurso compartido estaba en reposo.

records.source: A registry row does not require importing its screen. :mod:`spacr.qt.app_catalog` declares the key, the name, the sentence, the section, the stage and the name of the screen factory, and :func:`spacr.qt.app_catalog.register_declared` registers all of that without importing anything; the screen is imported the first time somebody opens it. A screen that contributes a stylesheet block registers it at that import, and ``MainWindow`` applies missing registered blocks to the new screen's own QSS scope before inserting it into the visible stack. :data:`spacr.qt.theme.WIDGET_QSS_MODULES` remains the inventory used when an exhaustive/static stylesheet is explicitly requested.
records.translation: Una fila del registro no requiere importar su pantalla. :mod:`spacr.qt.app_catalog` declara la clave, el nombre, la frase, la sección, la etapa y el nombre de la fábrica de la pantalla, y :func:`spacr.qt.app_catalog.register_declared` registra todo eso sin importar nada; la pantalla se importa la primera vez que alguien la abre. Una pantalla que aporta un bloque de hoja de estilos lo registra en esa importación, y ``MainWindow`` aplica los bloques registrados que falten al ámbito QSS propio de la nueva pantalla antes de insertarla en la pila visible. :data:`spacr.qt.theme.WIDGET_QSS_MODULES` sigue siendo el inventario que se usa cuando se solicita explícitamente una hoja de estilos exhaustiva o estática.

Hiding spaCR's own widgets and restoring them afterwards means remembering what was visible, what had focus, which docks were open and what the splitters were set to -- and getting any of it wrong leaves the user's layout rearranged by something that was meant to be a screensaver. records.translation: UNA VENTANA APARTE, no la principal puesta a pantalla completa. records.context: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the main GUI execution path.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is made once, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and its duration is logged. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the main GUI execution path against the real stack.
records.label: spacr.qt.sound#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the GUI thread.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is made once, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and its duration is logged. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the GUI thread against the real stack.
records.translation: **Qt Multimedia solo se toca en el hilo de la GUI.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` posee ``QMediaDevices`` y cada ``QSoundEffect`` y vive donde está el bucle de eventos de la aplicación; el ``QThread`` dedicado se queda con la parte realmente lenta, que es sintetizar un conjunto de sonidos (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy y escrituras de archivos, nada de Qt Multimedia). Conectarse al servidor de sonido es lento -- 354 ms medidos en una estación de trabajo con PipeWire --, así que se hace una vez, en un temporizador de inactividad tras activar el sonido (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), y su duración se registra. Reproducir un sonido ya cargado es ``play()``, que vuelve de inmediato: 0.007-0.014 ms en el hilo de la GUI con la pila real.

records.context: The rule follows from a crash. Building the effects on the audio independent execution path instead does move the connection off the main GUI execution path -- but Qt Multimedia's device handling belongs to the independent execution path that owns the event loop, so with the FFmpeg backend it enables socket notifiers from the wrong independent execution path. Reopening Preferences with sound on then segfaults, or wedges the interface with an empty Preferences frame until it is force quit.
records.label: spacr.qt.sound#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rule follows from a crash. Building the effects on the audio thread instead does move the connection off the GUI thread -- but Qt Multimedia's device handling belongs to the thread that owns the event loop, so with the FFmpeg backend it enables socket notifiers from the wrong thread. Reopening Preferences with sound on then segfaults, or wedges the interface with an empty Preferences frame until it is force quit.
records.translation: La regla se deriva de un fallo. Construir los efectos en el hilo de audio sí saca la conexión del hilo de la GUI -- pero la gestión de dispositivos de Qt Multimedia pertenece al hilo que posee el bucle de eventos, de modo que con el backend FFmpeg activa notificadores de socket desde el hilo equivocado. Volver a abrir Preferences con el sonido activado provoca entonces un fallo de segmentación, o bloquea la interfaz con un marco de Preferences vacío hasta que se fuerza su cierre.

records.source: The heartbeat is the measurement. A ``QTimer`` on the GUI thread bumps an integer; a daemon thread watches the integer. records.translation: El latido es la medida. Un ``QTimer`` en el hilo de la GUI incrementa un entero; un hilo demonio vigila el entero. records.source: Qt normally reports only that a timer cannot start from another thread, without naming the responsible object or call site. This module wraps the timer entry points and logs a Python stack when that condition occurs. The recorded stacks can also be attached to a crash report if the process exits before the log is reviewed.
records.translation: Normalmente Qt solo informa de que un temporizador no puede iniciarse desde otro hilo, sin nombrar el objeto responsable ni el punto de llamada. Este módulo envuelve los puntos de entrada de los temporizadores y registra una pila de Python cuando se da esa condición. Las pilas registradas también pueden adjuntarse a un informe de fallo si el proceso termina antes de que se revise el registro.

Qt refuses whenever they differ, which happens both ways round -- a worker touching a GUI object, and the main GUI execution path touching a worker-affine object; the second is easier to write by accident because the code reads as ordinary main GUI execution path code.

records.source: Makes the same test Qt makes: is the object's own thread the calling thread? Qt refuses whenever they differ, which happens both ways round -- a worker touching a GUI object, and the GUI thread touching a worker-affine object; the second is easier to write by accident because the code reads as ordinary GUI-thread code.
records.translation: Hace la misma comprobación que hace Qt: ¿es el propio hilo del objeto el hilo que llama? Qt se niega siempre que difieren, lo que ocurre en ambos sentidos -- un proceso de trabajo que toca un objeto de la GUI, y el hilo de la GUI que toca un objeto con afinidad a un proceso de trabajo; lo segundo es más fácil de escribir por accidente porque el código parece código ordinario del hilo de la GUI.

records.source: Rescues for a magic-wand flood that runs away.
records.translation: Rescates para un relleno de varita mágica que se desborda.

records.context: A flood fill from one click is the fastest way to take a whole object, and it has one failure mode that matters: the object touches something bright that is not it -- a debris streak, a saturated membrane seam, the rim of a well -- and the flood walks out along that seam and swallows the microscope field of view. The tolerance that takes the object correctly and the tolerance that escapes are often the same number, so "lower the tolerance" is not an answer: it shrinks the object as well.
records.label: spacr.qt.wand_rescue#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A flood fill from one click is the fastest way to take a whole object, and it has one failure mode that matters: the object touches something bright that is not it -- a debris streak, a saturated membrane seam, the rim of a well -- and the flood walks out along that seam and swallows the field. The tolerance that takes the object correctly and the tolerance that escapes are often the same number, so "lower the tolerance" is not an answer: it shrinks the object as well.
records.translation: Un relleno por inundación a partir de un clic es la forma más rápida de tomar un objeto entero, y tiene un modo de fallo que importa: el objeto toca algo brillante que no es él -- una estela de residuos, una costura de membrana saturada, el borde de un pocillo -- y el relleno sale a lo largo de esa costura y se traga el campo. La tolerancia que toma el objeto correctamente y la tolerancia que se escapa suelen ser el mismo número, así que "lower the tolerance" (bajar la tolerancia) no es una respuesta: también encoge el objeto.

records.context: Three independent rescues are offered here, in the order they run. Each catches the runaway at a different point, and each can be turned off:
records.label: spacr.qt.wand_rescue#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Three independent rescues are offered here, in the order they run. Each catches the runaway at a different point, and each can be turned off:
records.translation: Aquí se ofrecen tres rescates independientes, en el orden en que se ejecutan. Cada uno detecta el desbordamiento en un punto distinto, y cada uno se puede desactivar:

records.context: 1. **Directional runaway detection and trimming** — :func:`trim_directional_runaway` measures flood width along scanlines extending from the seed. A sustained abrupt expansion marks a leak, and pixels beyond that position are removed. Detection at this stage enables the following two refinements. 2. **Intensity-constrained reflooding** — :func:`wand_region` performs a binary search for the highest tested tolerance that does not trigger runaway detection. The resulting connected region replaces the straight-line directional cut. 3. **Gradient-based boundary refinement** — :func:`taper_region_to_intensity` applies a watershed to a smoothed intensity gradient within a configurable band, moving the provisional boundary toward a nearby image edge.
records.label: spacr.qt.wand_rescue#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. **Directional runaway detection and trimming** — :func:`trim_directional_runaway` measures flood width along scanlines extending from the seed. A sustained abrupt expansion marks a leak, and pixels beyond that position are removed. Detection at this stage enables the following two refinements. 2. **Intensity-constrained reflooding** — :func:`wand_region` performs a binary search for the highest tested tolerance that does not trigger runaway detection. The resulting connected region replaces the straight-line directional cut. 3. **Gradient-based boundary refinement** — :func:`taper_region_to_intensity` applies a watershed to a smoothed intensity gradient within a configurable band, moving the provisional boundary toward a nearby image edge.
records.translation: 1. **Detección y recorte de desbordamientos direccionales** — :func:`trim_directional_runaway` mide el ancho del relleno a lo largo de líneas de barrido que parten de la semilla. Una expansión brusca y sostenida marca una fuga, y se eliminan los píxeles más allá de esa posición. La detección en esta etapa habilita los dos refinamientos siguientes. 2. **Nuevo relleno restringido por intensidad** — :func:`wand_region` realiza una búsqueda binaria de la tolerancia probada más alta que no activa la detección de desbordamiento. La región conexa resultante sustituye el corte direccional en línea recta. 3. **Refinamiento del contorno basado en el gradiente** — :func:`taper_region_to_intensity` aplica un watershed a un gradiente de intensidad suavizado dentro de una banda configurable, desplazando el contorno provisional hacia un borde cercano de la imagen.

records.context: A directional cut is a straight line and a geodesic cap is a circular arc; objects are neither. ``provisional`` is whichever of those the earlier rescues produced. Its interior, inset by ``foreground_erode``, is marked as certainly object; the part of ``flooded_region`` that was thrown away, at least ``margin`` deep, is marked as certainly not. A watershed on the ``sigma``-smoothed intensity gradient decides the band between them, so the final boundary follows an intensity change -- up or down -- instead of the cut.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A directional cut is a straight line and a geodesic cap is a circular arc; objects are neither. ``provisional`` is whichever of those the earlier rescues produced. Its interior, inset by ``foreground_erode``, is marked as certainly object; the part of ``flooded_region`` that was thrown away, at least ``margin`` deep, is marked as certainly not. A watershed on the ``sigma``-smoothed intensity gradient decides the band between them, so the final boundary follows an intensity change -- up or down -- instead of the cut.
records.translation: Un corte direccional es una línea recta y un límite geodésico es un arco circular; los objetos no son ninguna de las dos cosas. ``provisional`` es cualquiera de esos que hayan producido los rescates anteriores. Su interior, reducido en ``foreground_erode``, se marca como objeto con certeza; la parte de ``flooded_region`` que se descartó, con al menos ``margin`` de profundidad, se marca como no objeto con certeza. records.context: Qt normally destroys a widget tree with its parent. pyqtgraph context menus are an exception: ``PlotItem`` and ``ViewBox`` intentionally create them as top-level windows and keep them through Python references. records.source: Qt normally destroys a widget tree with its parent. pyqtgraph context menus are an exception: ``PlotItem`` and ``ViewBox`` intentionally create them as top-level windows and keep them through Python references. Closing a screen therefore used to leave hundreds of live menu widgets behind, all of which a later palette change had to visit.
records.translation: Normalmente Qt destruye un árbol de widgets junto con su padre. Los menús contextuales de pyqtgraph son una excepción: ``PlotItem`` y ``ViewBox`` los crean intencionadamente como ventanas de nivel superior y los mantienen mediante referencias de Python. records.context: The masthead builds this label with ``setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy.Maximum, ...)`` and ``setMinimumWidth(0)`` and documents the intent -- the blurb "may shrink below its ideal width rather than force the window wider". Neither call achieves it: ``qSmartMinSize`` takes a shrinkable widget's minimum from ``minimumSizeHint()``, which for a non-wrapping ``QLabel`` is the width of the entire sentence, and it only lets an explicit ``minimumWidth`` override that when the value is greater than zero. Without this override the blurb, the one masthead control that can lose text harmlessly, gave up no width.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.api_help_label.ApiHelpLabel.minimumSizeHint#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The masthead builds this label with ``setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy.Maximum, ...)`` and ``setMinimumWidth(0)`` and documents the intent -- the blurb "may shrink below its ideal width rather than force the window wider". Neither call achieves it: ``qSmartMinSize`` takes a shrinkable widget's minimum from ``minimumSizeHint()``, which for a non-wrapping ``QLabel`` is the width of the entire sentence, and it only lets an explicit ``minimumWidth`` override that when the value is greater than zero. Without this override the blurb, the one masthead control that can lose text harmlessly, gave up no width.
records.translation: La cabecera construye esta etiqueta con ``setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy.Maximum, ...)`` y ``setMinimumWidth(0)`` y documenta la intención -- la entradilla "puede reducirse por debajo de su ancho ideal en lugar de obligar a ensanchar la ventana". Ninguna de las dos llamadas lo consigue: ``qSmartMinSize`` toma el mínimo de un widget reducible de ``minimumSizeHint()``, que para una ``QLabel`` sin ajuste de línea es el ancho de toda la frase, y solo permite que un ``minimumWidth`` explícito lo sustituya cuando el valor es mayor que cero. Sin esta sustitución, la entradilla, el único control de la cabecera que puede perder texto sin perjuicio, no cedía ningún ancho.

records.context: Barcode regexes are not filename regexes.  The sequencing workflow requires three specifically named capture groups (``columnID``, ``grna`` and ``rowID``), so the generic filename-regex editor cannot validate this field. records.source: Barcode regexes are not filename regexes.  The sequencing pipeline requires three specifically named capture groups (``columnID``, ``grna`` and ``rowID``), so the generic filename-regex editor cannot validate this field. This module keeps the compact settings row while providing a focused dialog that compiles the expression and previews its captures against a pasted read.
records.translation: Las expresiones regulares de códigos de barras no son expresiones de nombres de archivo. El pipeline de secuenciación requiere tres grupos de captura con nombres específicos (``columnID``, ``grna`` y ``rowID``), por lo que el editor genérico de expresiones regulares de nombres de archivo no puede validar este campo. Este módulo mantiene la fila de ajustes compacta y ofrece un diálogo específico que compila la expresión y muestra una vista previa de sus capturas sobre una lectura pegada.

records.context: ``QColorDialog.getColor`` defaults to the *platform's* colour chooser. On a GNOME desktop with ``xdg-desktop-portal`` running, that is not a Qt widget at all: Qt asks the portal, the portal starts (or wakes) the GTK implementation over D-Bus, and the dialog can be slow to appear. Every colour picker in the tree was reached through an unguarded ``getColor`` — six of them, none passing ``DontUseNativeDialog``.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.colour_picker#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``QColorDialog.getColor`` defaults to the *platform's* colour chooser. On a GNOME desktop with ``xdg-desktop-portal`` running, that is not a Qt widget at all: Qt asks the portal, the portal starts (or wakes) the GTK implementation over D-Bus, and the dialog can be slow to appear. Every colour picker in the tree was reached through an unguarded ``getColor`` — six of them, none passing ``DontUseNativeDialog``.
records.translation: ``QColorDialog.getColor`` usa por defecto el selector de color *de la plataforma*. En un escritorio GNOME con ``xdg-desktop-portal`` en ejecución, eso ni siquiera es un widget de Qt: Qt consulta al portal, el portal inicia (o despierta) la implementación de GTK mediante D-Bus, y el diálogo puede tardar en aparecer. A todos los selectores de color del árbol se llegaba mediante un ``getColor`` sin protección — seis en total, ninguno de los cuales pasaba ``DontUseNativeDialog``.

records.source: Qt's own dialog opens immediately, looks the same on every platform, and follows the application palette — which the GTK one does not.
records.translation: El diálogo propio de Qt se abre de inmediato, tiene el mismo aspecto en todas las plataformas y sigue la paleta de la aplicación — cosa que el de GTK no hace.

records.context: The portal round trip **cannot be reproduced headless**: an offscreen Qt never asks the portal, so no test in this suite can observe the stall or its absence. The restyle work itself is free (``set_line_style`` 0.000 s on a 1,200 point plot) so the wait is in the dialog — and "the portal is what the wait is" is a named, checkable hypothesis to be confirmed on a real display, not something this file proves. What IS proven here, by ``tests/qt/test_colour_picker.py``, is that no call site can ask for the platform dialog any more.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.colour_picker#4

records.source: The portal round trip **cannot be reproduced headless**: an offscreen Qt never asks the portal, so no test in this suite can observe the stall or its absence. The restyle work itself is free (``set_line_style`` 0.000 s on a 1,200 point plot) so the wait is in the dialog — and "the portal is what the wait is" is a named, checkable hypothesis to be confirmed on a real display, not something this file proves. What IS proven here, by ``tests/qt/test_colour_picker.py``, is that no call site can ask for the platform dialog any more.
records.translation: El viaje de ida y vuelta al portal **no se puede reproducir sin interfaz**: un Qt fuera de pantalla nunca consulta al portal, así que ninguna prueba de este conjunto puede observar el bloqueo ni su ausencia. El trabajo de cambio de estilo en sí no cuesta nada (``set_line_style`` 0.000 s en un gráfico de 1,200 puntos), así que la espera está en el diálogo — y "la espera es el portal" es una hipótesis concreta y comprobable que debe confirmarse en una pantalla real, no algo que demuestre este archivo. Lo que SÍ se demuestra aquí, mediante ``tests/qt/test_colour_picker.py``, es que ningún punto de llamada puede ya pedir el diálogo de la plataforma.

records.context: Why it is a second entry rather than a backend switch. The CPU path jitters four samples ACROSS four frames, which averages four different animation times; a GPU pass can afford the four samples inside one instant. They are not the same picture, so offering them as one option with a hidden backend would mean the same setting drawing two things. "Orbit fold" is taken, so this is "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- descriptive of what actually differs rather than a version number.

records.source: WHY IT IS A SECOND ENTRY RATHER THAN A BACKEND SWITCH. The CPU path jitters four samples ACROSS four frames, which averages four different animation times; a GPU pass can afford the four samples inside one instant. They are not the same picture, so offering them as one option with a hidden backend would mean the same setting drawing two things. "Orbit fold" is taken, so this is "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- descriptive of what actually differs rather than a version number.
records.translation: POR QUÉ ES UNA SEGUNDA ENTRADA Y NO UN CAMBIO DE BACKEND. La ruta de CPU reparte cuatro muestras A LO LARGO de cuatro fotogramas, lo que promedia cuatro tiempos de animación distintos; una pasada en GPU puede permitirse las cuatro muestras dentro de un mismo instante. No son la misma imagen, así que ofrecerlas como una sola opción con un backend oculto haría que el mismo ajuste dibujara dos cosas. "Orbit fold" ya está ocupado, así que este es "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- que describe lo que realmente difiere en lugar de un número de versión.

records.translation: Divididos según DE QUÉ trata el ajuste, no según qué widget lo lee:

records.context: ``General`` How much data is loaded and how the cloud is drawn. The sampling setting lives here because it is the answer to the module being laggy on a real dataset -- a screen of a million objects is slow to draw, slow to hit-test, and no more informative than a fifth of them. ``2D`` Data-selection filtering on a scatter: the tools, the shapes, and the clustering that proposes shapes for you. ``3D`` Data-selection filtering in a volume. The settings are here; the workspace they drive is the next piece of work.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.gate_settings#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``General`` How much data is loaded and how the cloud is drawn. The sampling setting lives here because it is the answer to the module being laggy on a real dataset -- a screen of a million objects is slow to draw, slow to hit-test, and no more informative than a fifth of them. ``2D`` Gating on a scatter: the tools, the shapes, and the clustering that proposes shapes for you. ``3D`` Gating in a volume. The settings are here; the workspace they drive is the next piece of work.
records.translation: ``General`` Cuántos datos se cargan y cómo se dibuja la nube. El ajuste de muestreo está aquí porque es la respuesta a la lentitud del módulo con un conjunto de datos real -- una pantalla con un millón de objetos es lenta de dibujar, lenta en la detección de clics y no más informativa que una quinta parte de ellos. ``2D`` Aplicación de compuertas sobre un diagrama de dispersión: las herramientas, las formas y el agrupamiento que propone formas por usted. ``3D`` Aplicación de compuertas en un volumen. Los ajustes están aquí; el espacio de trabajo que controlan es la siguiente tarea pendiente.

records.source: Every setting is a field on :class:`GateEditorSettings`, which is a plain frozen dataclass -- no Qt -- so what the editor does with a setting can be tested without building a dialog, and so the whole set can be written to disk as one thing later.
records.translation: Cada ajuste es un campo de :class:`GateEditorSettings`, que es una dataclass congelada simple -- sin Qt --, de modo que lo que hace el editor con un ajuste se puede probar sin construir un diálogo, y todo el conjunto se podrá escribir en disco más adelante como una sola cosa.

records.context: **Sampling is a display concern only.** A data-selection boundary drawn on 20% of the objects is still a statement about all of them; the export re-reads the full table and applies the data-selection boundary there (:func:`spacr.filters.gate_mask_over_table`). Nothing downstream of the plot ever sees the sample.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.gate_settings#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Sampling is a display concern only.** A gate drawn on 20% of the objects is still a statement about all of them; the export re-reads the full table and applies the gate there (:func:`spacr.filters.gate_mask_over_table`). Nothing downstream of the plot ever sees the sample.
records.translation: **El muestreo solo afecta a la visualización.** Una compuerta dibujada sobre el 20% de los objetos sigue siendo una afirmación sobre todos ellos; la exportación vuelve a leer la tabla completa y aplica allí la compuerta (:func:`spacr.filters.gate_mask_over_table`). Nada posterior al gráfico ve nunca la muestra.

Neither knows about the Mask module; the live preview hands in its session's masks and its microscope field of view, and draws the answer.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.mask_comparison#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The module has two parts. :func:`composite` is the arithmetic, on plain arrays, so the picture a user sees can be checked pixel by pixel against a hand calculation. :class:`MaskComparisonDialog` is the popup that chooses what goes into it. Neither knows about the Mask module; the live preview hands in its session's masks and its field, and draws the answer.
records.translation: El módulo tiene dos partes. :func:`composite` es la aritmética, sobre matrices simples, para que la imagen que ve el usuario pueda comprobarse píxel a píxel con un cálculo a mano. :class:`MaskComparisonDialog` es la ventana emergente que elige qué entra en ella. Ninguna de las dos sabe nada del módulo Mask; la vista previa en directo pasa las máscaras de su sesión y su campo, y dibuja la respuesta.

records.context: Layers are composited with the "over" operator, bottom first. The canvas starts black. Each ticked layer, bottom first, is laid on with its opacity ``a``: where it covers, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; where it does not, ``out`` is left alone. An image covers every pixel; a mask covers its objects only, so the background of a mask never dims what is under it. The result is rounded to the nearest whole grey level.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.mask_comparison#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Layers are composited with the "over" operator, bottom first. The canvas starts black. Each ticked layer, bottom first, is laid on with its opacity ``a``: where it covers, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; where it does not, ``out`` is left alone. An image covers every pixel; a mask covers its objects only, so the background of a mask never dims what is under it. The result is rounded to the nearest whole grey level.
records.translation: Las capas se componen con el operador "over", empezando por la de abajo. El lienzo empieza en negro. Cada capa marcada, empezando por la de abajo, se superpone con su opacidad ``a``: donde cubre, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; donde no cubre, ``out`` no se toca. Una imagen cubre todos los píxeles; una máscara solo cubre sus objetos, de modo que el fondo de una máscara nunca atenúa lo que hay debajo. El resultado se redondea al nivel de gris entero más cercano.

records.source: Split from :meth:`add_paths` so the GUI thread does not block on the filesystem. Everything here is a list of strings; the ``isdir`` and ``listdir`` that turn a dropped folder into files run on this widget's own worker (:func:`files_under`), because a drop is a path the user chose and on a microscope rig that is the share the images live on -- one stat under a sleeping ``autofs`` mount was measured at over twenty seconds, on the thread that paints.
records.translation: Separado de :meth:`add_paths` para que el hilo de la GUI no se bloquee con el sistema de archivos. Todo aquí es una lista de cadenas; el ``isdir`` y el ``listdir`` que convierten una carpeta soltada en archivos se ejecutan en el propio proceso de trabajo de este widget (:func:`files_under`), porque lo que se suelta es una ruta que eligió el usuario y, en un equipo de microscopía, es el recurso compartido en el que están las imágenes -- se midió que un solo stat bajo un montaje ``autofs`` en reposo tardaba más de veinte segundos, en el hilo que pinta.

records.context: When a dataset's laboratory microplate / microplate sample position / microscope field of view / channel assignment is *inferred* — from a container file's internal structure or from a folder layout — the guess is rarely perfect. records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.metadata_table#1

records.source: When a dataset's plate / well / field / channel assignment is *inferred* — from a container file's internal structure or from a folder layout — the guess is rarely perfect. This widget shows those inferred rows in an editable :class:`QTableWidget` so the user can correct wells, split conditions, relabel channels, etc. before committing, then writes a ``filename_map.csv`` the pipeline consumes.
records.translation: Cuando la asignación de placa / pocillo / campo / canal de un conjunto de datos se *infiere* — a partir de la estructura interna de un archivo contenedor o de una disposición de carpetas —, la suposición rara vez es perfecta. Este widget muestra esas filas inferidas en una :class:`QTableWidget` editable para que el usuario pueda corregir pocillos, separar condiciones, cambiar la etiqueta de los canales, etc. antes de confirmar, y después escribe un ``filename_map.csv`` que consume el pipeline.

records.context: The grid in :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid` edits values; the settings panel is a key-value mapping of widgets, and the workflow reads the widgets. Mounting the grid without a binding would give an application view two answers to the same question -- the table showing what the user typed and ``collect()`` still returning what the widget holds -- and the processing session would silently use the second one, so the saved settings would differ from what the grid shows.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.object_grid_binding#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The grid in :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid` edits values; the settings panel is a dictionary of widgets, and the pipeline reads the widgets. Mounting the grid without a binding would give a screen two answers to the same question -- the table showing what the user typed and ``collect()`` still returning what the widget holds -- and the run would silently use the second one, so the saved settings would differ from what the grid shows.
records.translation: La cuadrícula de :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid` edita valores; el panel de ajustes es un diccionario de widgets, y el pipeline lee los widgets. Montar la cuadrícula sin un enlace daría a una pantalla dos respuestas a la misma pregunta -- la tabla mostrando lo que escribió el usuario y ``collect()`` devolviendo todavía lo que contiene el widget --, y la ejecución usaría en silencio la segunda, de modo que los ajustes guardados diferirían de lo que muestra la cuadrícula.

records.context: So the grid never becomes the source of truth. It is a view that writes through: every edit lands in the widget behind it, and the widget stays what the workflow reads. Nothing downstream of ``collect()`` learns that the grid exists, so no settings file, notebook or ``spacr-run`` invocation changes.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.object_grid_binding#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So the grid never becomes the source of truth. It is a view that writes through: every edit lands in the widget behind it, and the widget stays what the pipeline reads. Nothing downstream of ``collect()`` learns that the grid exists, so no settings file, notebook or ``spacr-run`` invocation changes.
records.translation: Por eso la cuadrícula nunca se convierte en la fuente de verdad. Es una vista que escribe a través: cada edición llega al widget que hay detrás, y el widget sigue siendo lo que lee el pipeline. Nada posterior a ``collect()`` sabe que existe la cuadrícula, de modo que no cambia ningún archivo de ajustes, cuaderno ni invocación de ``spacr-run``.

records.source: The re-entrancy guard is what stops the table visibly rebuilding under a cursor that is still in a cell: writing a value into a widget makes that widget emit, and a screen that reseeds the grid on every widget change would rebuild it mid-edit. No value depends on the guard -- the write reads the grid once, before the first widget moves -- so a reseed halfway cannot drop an edit either way.
records.translation: La protección contra la reentrada es lo que impide que la tabla se reconstruya visiblemente bajo un cursor que todavía está en una celda: escribir un valor en un widget hace que ese widget emita una señal, y una pantalla que vuelve a sembrar la cuadrícula en cada cambio de widget la reconstruiría a mitad de una edición. Ningún valor depende de la protección -- la escritura lee la cuadrícula una vez, antes de que se mueva el primer widget --, así que una nueva siembra a mitad de camino tampoco puede perder una edición.

records.context: Windows opened from the preview are not scaled with it. A dialog parented to the panel is a window of its own, yet Qt cascades the panel's scaled sheet into it, and the walk found it among the panel's children: at 150 % a settings dialog's buttons were 59 px tall, not the 40 px of every other dialog. Such a window and everything in it are kept at 100 %, and the window's own sheet re-states, at 100 %, the sizes it would otherwise inherit scaled -- set as it is polished, so before it is first laid out.

Such a window and everything in it are kept at 100 %, and the window's own sheet re-states, at 100 %, the sizes it would otherwise inherit scaled -- set as it is polished, so before it is first laid out.
records.translation: Las ventanas (Windows, en el sentido de ventanas de la interfaz) abiertas desde la vista previa no se escalan con ella. Un diálogo que tiene el panel como padre es una ventana propia, pero Qt le transmite en cascada la hoja escalada del panel, y el recorrido lo encontraba entre los hijos del panel: al 150 %, los botones de un diálogo de ajustes medían 59 px de alto, no los 40 px de todos los demás diálogos. Una ventana así, y todo lo que contiene, se mantiene al 100 %, y la hoja propia de la ventana vuelve a declarar, al 100 %, los tamaños que de otro modo heredaría escalados -- establecida en el momento de pulirse, es decir, antes de su primera disposición.

records.context: An owner can replace renderers. The default renderers draw a plain overlay, categorical masks, the flows as Cellpose hands them and the probability on the magma scale. An owner with its own idea of an outline -- the live preview's colour choice and thickness -- registers a renderer for that view with :meth:`SegmentationViews.set_renderer` and keeps the other three. A renderer answers with a picture, with a sentence to show in the picture's place, or with ``None`` for the widget's own "nothing yet" sentence.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.segmentation_views#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: An owner can replace renderers. The default renderers draw a plain overlay, categorical masks, the flows as Cellpose hands them and the probability on the magma scale. An owner with its own idea of an outline -- the live preview's colour choice and thickness -- registers a renderer for that view with :meth:`SegmentationViews.set_renderer` and keeps the other three. A renderer answers with a picture, with a sentence to show in the picture's place, or with ``None`` for the widget's own "nothing yet" sentence.
records.translation: Un propietario puede sustituir los representadores. Los representadores predeterminados dibujan una superposición simple, máscaras categóricas, los flujos tal como los entrega Cellpose y la probabilidad en la escala magma. Un propietario con su propia idea de un contorno -- la elección de color y el grosor de la vista previa en directo -- registra un representador para esa vista con :meth:`SegmentationViews.set_renderer` y conserva los otros tres. Un representador responde con una imagen, con una frase que mostrar en lugar de la imagen o con ``None`` para la frase "nothing yet" (aún nada) propia del widget.

records.translation: El lienzo es intercambiable. records.source: The read limit sets the download size. The four runs are 20.4 GB in full; a hundred thousand reads from each is about 30 MB, because ENA serves gzipped FASTQ that :func:`spacr.sra.fetch_reads` reads as a stream and abandons once it has enough. The estimate is shown before anything starts and is recomputed as the limit changes, so the size is known before the download begins.
records.translation: El límite de lecturas determina el tamaño de la descarga. Las cuatro ejecuciones ocupan 20.4 GB completas; cien mil lecturas de cada una son unos 30 MB, porque ENA sirve FASTQ comprimido con gzip que :func:`spacr.sra.fetch_reads` lee como un flujo y abandona en cuanto tiene suficiente. La estimación se muestra antes de que empiece nada y se vuelve a calcular cuando cambia el límite, de modo que el tamaño se conoce antes de que empiece la descarga.

records.context: What this module adds is the tie. Two views of the same region are only worth putting side by side if they stay in register: a curator comparing a field with its enhanced self is looking for a difference between them, and a difference in where the two are pointing is the one difference that is not information. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` makes a group of views share one zoom and one scroll position, so zooming or panning any of them moves all of them.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.zoom_view#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: What this module adds is the tie. Two views of the same region are only worth putting side by side if they stay in register: a curator comparing a field with its enhanced self is looking for a difference between them, and a difference in where the two are pointing is the one difference that is not information. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` makes a group of views share one zoom and one scroll position, so zooming or panning any of them moves all of them.
records.translation: Lo que añade este módulo es el vínculo. Dos vistas de la misma región solo merecen ponerse una junto a otra si se mantienen alineadas: un responsable de la curación que compara un campo con su versión mejorada busca una diferencia entre ellas, y una diferencia en el lugar al que apuntan ambas es la única diferencia que no aporta información. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` hace que un grupo de vistas compartan un mismo zoom y una misma posición de desplazamiento, de modo que ampliar o desplazar cualquiera de ellas las mueve todas.
